title: Exact quantum circuits for lattice Boltzmann realization of the Dirac equation
authors: Nilesh Sawant, Ethan Young, Kevin Griffin, Michael Martin
abstract: The quantum lattice Boltzmann (QLB) scheme of Succi and Dellar advances a four-component Dirac spinor on a lattice by a fixed sequence of local, exactly norm-preserving operations: a basis rotation, a collision, a streaming shift, and the inverse rotation. This unitarity is a structural property of the scheme, not an approximation, which suggests that a QLB time step should map onto a sequence of quantum gates. Here we make that mapping explicit. We give a gate-level construction of every operation of the three-dimensional Dirac QLB scheme: the fixed rotation gates, the collision gate, the streaming shift as a controlled increment on a position register, the position-dependent potential as a phase oracle, and periodic and reflecting (bounce-back) boundary conditions as unitary circuits. We then compose them into single-axis, two- and three-dimensional time steps. On a state-vector emulator the resulting circuits reproduce the classical QLB solver to machine precision (maximum density deviation between $3.7\times10^{-12}$ and $1.0\times10^{-17}$ across the one-, two-, and three-dimensional tests), so the circuits are the scheme rather than an approximation of it. The scope is narrow: we establish that the Succi-Dellar theory can be implemented on a (gate-model) quantum computer, and report the associated gate counts. We make no claim of computational advantage; state preparation, measurement, and asymptotic cost are discussed as open questions. All operators, circuits, tests, and figures are reproducible from the open-source quantumKineticMethods library.
summary: This paper translates the classical Quantum Lattice Boltzmann method for solving the Dirac equation into an exact sequence of quantum gates. By mapping every physical step—including streaming and collision—to specific unitary circuits, the authors prove that this complex simulation can be run on a gate-model quantum computer. This work establishes a blueprint for simulating relativistic fermionic dynamics using quantum computation.
main_problem: To determine if the Succi–Dellar Dirac Quantum Lattice Boltzmann (QLB) scheme can be written exactly as a quantum circuit.
main_result: The authors provide an exact, gate-level construction for every operation of the 3D Dirac QLB scheme, reproducing classical results to machine precision on state-vector emulators.
method: They map each elementary physical operation (rotation, collision, streaming shift) into a sequence of fundamental quantum gates and circuits.
model_or_system: The model is the Dirac equation solved via the QLB scheme on a lattice. The simulation uses amplitude encoding across separate spinor and position registers to represent the field state.
key_observables: Density deviation (reproduced to machine precision), particle velocity ($v_g$), group velocities, and mean speed relative to $c$.
important_parameters: Lattice size ($N$), dimensionless mass ($	ilde{m}$), potential couplings, and the number of qubits required ($\propto \log N$).
main_assumptions: The scope is limited to establishing implementability on a gate-model quantum computer; state preparation and measurement costs are left as open questions.
figures_summary: References include comparisons of classical vs. qubit circuit implementations, and analysis showing how oblique motion slows massless particles below $c$ in 2D/3D lattices compared to continuum estimates.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the unitary nature of the QLB steps, then provides gate-level constructions for all components (rotation, collision, shift). It verifies these circuits on emulators across 1D, 2D, and 3D tests before discussing physical implications like velocity dispersion.
why_interesting: It demonstrates a concrete pathway to implementing complex, non-equilibrium quantum dynamics (like Dirac evolution) directly using known quantum gate primitives, which is crucial for developing quantum simulation algorithms beyond simple Hamiltonians.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
